moduleTitle: Lesson 1 - Preparing your Project for using TDS
learningObjectives: Check matching Tosca and Tosca Server versions and installation prerequisites.
Open Test Data Management and distinguish repository database settings from TDS type names.
Compare persistent SQLite storage with temporary InMemory storage.
Configure TestDataEndpoint and TestDataRepository with the intended scope and security requirements.

elements.description: Use matching Tosca and Tosca Server versions. Before installing, check administrator rights, the current system requirements and available service ports. Test Data Service is included in Tosca Server.

elements.text: This guide uses current documentation rather than an unverified Academy installation video or downloadable exercise subset.

elements.description: Install through the setup dialog or unattended mode, then configure the required services with Tricentis Service Configuration. Do not assume setup automatically opens every service page.

bulletPoints: Tosca and Tosca Server must have the same version number.
Check installation prerequisites and service configuration before using TDS.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Accessing the Test Data Management page

elements.description: Open http(s)://<DNS name of the Tosca Server machine>:<Tosca Gateway port>. In HTTPS setups use the certificate name and sign in with Tricentis User Administration credentials.

Open Test Data Management from the server interface and select a repository tile. Repository access may depend on your user groups when authorization is enabled. A visible tile does not grant unrestricted administration rights.
Create Repository defines a unique name and database settings. InMemory, SQLite, MSSQL and Oracle are supported; the available connection fields depend on the selected type.

elements.title: Choose storage deliberately
items: SQLite persists data in a file; provide an appropriate database location.
InMemory is temporary: restarting the server loses its contents.
MSSQL and Oracle need their database connection settings. Description is optional and limited to 200 characters.

elements.text: A repository and a TDS type inside it are different objects. The Standard Modules document forbidden characters for TDS type names; do not present that rule as a verified repository-name rule.
Creation requires the relevant service and database permissions. Test the connection and verify the saved configuration before writing practice data.

bulletPoints: Database type determines storage and connection settings.
Use a disposable repository for independent practice.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Connecting Tosca Commander to the repository

elements.description: The documented prerequisites use Standard.tsu. In its Configurations folder, select TestDataService. Set TestDataEndpoint to the service location and TestDataRepository to the intended repository.

Drop the configuration onto an object that supports TCPs, such as a TestCase, a TestCase folder or a ComponentFolder. Check the execution-side scope too; placing a configuration under one branch does not configure unrelated branches.
Children inherit TCPs from their parent. A lower-level value can override an inherited value. Use a shared configuration for a shared environment and scoped values where repositories differ.

elements.text: For HTTPS setups, follow the documented authentication procedure, including AuthenticationAccessKey and the Gateway endpoint. Where repository authorization is enabled, verify the required access. Endpoint and repository values alone are not an access grant.

bulletPoints: TestDataEndpoint selects the service location; TestDataRepository selects the repository.
Inspect inherited values on the objects you execute.

elements.text: Independent practice: create a disposable SQLite repository, assign its TestDataService configuration to a sample TestCase, and inspect the effective TCP values before running it. Academy exercises and a Tosca runtime execution have not been verified here.

examPitfalls.title: Mismatched versions
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Installing a Server version unrelated to the installed Tosca version.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use matching versions and check current installation prerequisites.

examPitfalls.title: Wrong configuration scope
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming one folder configuration automatically covers unrelated TestCase and execution branches.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect the effective inherited values and use scoped overrides where needed.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing naming and connection rules
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Applying TDS type-name restrictions to repository names, or using SQLite location fields for all database types.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Treat repositories and their item types separately; follow the settings for the selected database type.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team wants a repository whose data does NOT persist after the Tosca Server restarts. Which repository Type should they choose?

options.text: Neither type is available in TDS.

practiceQuiz.hint: One type is file-backed (persistent); the other lives only in RAM while the server runs.
practiceQuiz.rationale: InMemory contents are lost when the server restarts. SQLite is file-backed and keeps data across restarts.

optionExplanations.A: SQLite uses persistent file storage, so it is unsuitable for intentional loss on server restart.
optionExplanations.B: InMemory stores temporary data that is lost when the server restarts.
optionExplanations.C: The two types do not have equal persistence: SQLite keeps its file-backed contents.
optionExplanations.D: Both SQLite and InMemory are documented repository database types.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team needs the same TDS settings for several test objects. Which assignment approach is supported?

options.text: Assign the configuration to a ComponentFolder or to appropriate TestCase and execution objects, checking inheritance and scope.

practiceQuiz.hint: Configurations can be assigned to objects that support TCPs.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Configurations bundle TCPs and can be assigned to supported objects. Inheritance covers children, so check scope and any overrides on the objects that will execute.

optionExplanations.A: TCP assignment is not restricted to TestSteps; supported objects include TestCases and folders.
optionExplanations.B: These supported objects can receive configurations; inspect inheritance and scope for the intended tests.
optionExplanations.C: Shared configurations are supported; their effects follow the object scope and inherited values.
optionExplanations.D: The documentation lists many supported object types rather than only Requirements.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TDS type name avoids the forbidden characters documented for the Standard Modules?
practiceQuiz.hint: Check each type name for reserved punctuation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: CustomerDetails avoids the forbidden punctuation. The other choices contain #, square brackets or a semicolon. This is a TDS type-name rule, not a verified repository-name rule.

optionExplanations.A: The hash character is forbidden in a TDS type name.
optionExplanations.B: Both opening and closing square brackets are forbidden in TDS type names.
optionExplanations.C: CustomerDetails contains none of the documented forbidden type-name characters.
optionExplanations.D: A semicolon is forbidden in a TDS type name.

quickRecap.value: Use matching Tosca and Tosca Server versions and check prerequisites.
Use the Gateway URL, certificate name and required authentication.
SQLite persists; InMemory loses data on server restart. MSSQL and Oracle use connection settings.
A repository contains TDS types. Type-name restrictions are a separate rule.
Standard.tsu provides TestDataService; set TestDataEndpoint and TestDataRepository.
TCPs are inherited by children and can be overridden at a lower level. Check execution scope and access.
